title: feat(auctions): auction order details — settlement status display & auction-aware order actions (supersedes #1226)
body:
## Auction Order Details — settlement status display & auction-aware order actions

**This PR supersedes #1226.** It is the same feature work, re-based onto a fork branch and opened against `auctions` directly, minus the one commit in #1226 that was not part of porting auctions onto the order-details page.

Two reasons it is a new PR rather than a push to `feat/auction-order-details-v2`:

1. **Scope.** The feature branch carries `d0cbab80` *"add Product/Auction Type and Item title columns to order tables"* plus the three refs that exist only to serve it. `src/components/orders/orderColumns.tsx` feeds `/dashboard/sales/sales` **and** `/dashboard/account/your-purchases` — product and account surfaces, not the order-details page, and the chip it adds ("Product" / "Auction") applies to both tables. It is dropped here and needs its own PR and its own design.
2. **Mechanics.** The push account (`maxime-tt`) has no write access to `PlebeianApp/market`, so a cleaned history cannot be force-pushed onto `feat/auction-order-details-v2`. A fork PR against `auctions` is the route that can actually carry it.

Authorship of the feature is unchanged: commits 1–3 are @Franchovy's, 4–13 are @felixfelix-bot's, and their subjects are identical to `247f9a25`.

### Head state (updated 2026-09-25)

**Head:** `d1a4a647ddb87dfeb90f00de3cbb33c4d42d5285` — rebased onto the current `auctions` tip and adapted to ADR-0011 in the same pass.

Three things landed on the base after the last CI run, and this push absorbs all three:

- **ADR-0011 collateral verification (`#1280`)** gates bid validity on DLEQ evidence: without `dleqKeysets`
  every candidate bid classifies `pending`, no `canonicalWinner` is derived, and this feature's descriptor
  input resolved to nothing. The fixture now mints honest DLEQ proofs and passes the matching keyset, and
  `OrderDetailComponent` threads `useDleqKeysetPolling` into the descriptor input — the same hook the
  auction page and the settlement surfaces use. See the review response below.
- The rebase moved `e2e/scenarios/auctionOrderFixture.test.ts` out of the e2e harness into
  `src/lib/__tests__/auctionOrderFixture.test.ts`, so the gate runs in `bun run test:unit` **with no change to
  `package.json`** — which is the resolution of the maintainer's `CHANGES_REQUESTED` (that file is not
  touched by this branch at all).
- The gate now injects `mintKeysets`, so it never attempts a connection to the fixture mint URL.

### What this PR does

Extends `OrderDetailComponent` to detect auction orders (via the `a` tag with kind 30408) and render auction-specific UI instead of the generic product order view.

**`src/queries/orders.tsx`**
- `getAuctionCoordinatesFromOrder()` — extracts the auction coordinate from the order's `a` tag, `null` for non-auction orders
- `isAuctionOrder()` / `getAuctionOrderClassification()` — broad auction-associated detection, explicitly **presentation-only**

**`src/lib/auction/settlementDescriptor.ts`**
- `getAuctionFulfillmentAuthority()` — fulfillment authority derived from the *validated* settlement descriptor, never from the order's own buyer-authored claim marker
- `claimOrderAuthorizesFulfillment()` — binds that authority to the exact order id being mutated

**`src/components/orders/OrderDetailComponent.tsx`**
- auction detection, `AuctionCard` instead of `ProductCard`
- settlement status derived from `getSettlementDescriptor()` (ADR-0003 / ADR-0004) rather than `settlements[0]`, with the settlement card replacing the invoice/payment section
- `"Auction Item"` header instead of the product count

**`src/components/orders/OrderActions.tsx`**
- suppresses "Cancel Order" and "Confirm Payment Received" for auction orders and hides the stock dialog — the auction flow publishes no generic payment confirmation, and cancelling cannot release a bidder's locked proofs
- takes the fulfillment authority object from the validated settlement + canonical claim, so an auction claim order is fulfillment-ready while it is still `PENDING` (auction fulfillment must not be stranded behind a status the auction flow never publishes), and binds it to the order id being mutated

### Review items

**@maximotodev — 2026-08-10, four inline blockers** (at `9b35d72a`):

| Item | Addressed in |
|---|---|
| `settlements[0]` plus array presence treated as authoritative settlement/payment state (`OrderDetailComponent.tsx:138`) | `cabeea2f` (derive from the validated descriptor) → `f55e46ee` (fail closed on malformed/conflicting data; terminal `reserve_not_met`/`cancelled`/`griefed_no_fallback` represented without a path release) |
| `isAuction` only gated the stock dialog; generic predicates still exposed Cancel/Confirm for a `PENDING` claim | `02e97661` (suppress) + `b8166030` (authority from the canonical claim) + `f55e46ee` (settlement → claim → fulfillment-ready → Process → Ship → Receive/Complete) |
| broad auction detector must stay presentation-only, not authority | `f55e46ee` |
| positive auction fixture was not production-valid (open auction, reserve 1000 vs settlement 500, placeholder bid reference, missing production fields) | `048c7199` + `9b3facb7`, and `baea9ce4` wires the production-validator gate into the unit suite so the fixture cannot silently rot |
| `griefed_no_fallback` collapsed into the seller-cancelled case | `d9c52917` |

**@maximotodev — 2026-09-13 re-review, two P1s: both fixed in the head's new commit** (`fix(orders): bind auction fulfillment authority to its claim order, fail closed on pending`):

- **P1a — a `pending` settlement could still authorize fulfillment.** `deriveState()` retains a seller-signed kind-1024 that passed the seller/root/coordinate checks while its required matching path release is still unvalidated/unobserved; `classifyPhase()` reads `settled` from the status alone, so the helper returned `fulfillmentReady: true`. Authority is now derived from the positive classification `latestSettlementValidity === 'valid'` (carried out of `deriveState`), so `pending` fails closed exactly like `invalid` — and a future third validity value cannot silently unlock it.
- **P1b — authority was not bound to the order being mutated.** `OrderDetailComponent` collapsed the authority object to the boolean `auctionFulfillmentReady` before handing it to `OrderActions`, which then mutated `order.order.id` with no proof that this order id is the `claimOrderId` that earned the authority — so authority from claim A could unlock an auction-associated order B carrying the same coordinate. `OrderActions` now takes the authority **object** (`auctionAuthority`) and requires `claimOrderAuthorizesFulfillment(authority, order.order.id)` — `fulfillmentReady && claimOrderId === order.order.id` — before `Process` or `Mark As Shipped` is reachable for an auction order. Callers without validated context pass nothing, which stays fail-closed. Product orders are unchanged.
- **Merge precondition — rebase onto current `auctions`:** done. `#1247` landed after this branch was cut and turned the auction query results into plain event-like values, so `.rawEvent()` no longer exists on them; the descriptor input now goes through `toRawEvent()`. That call was a **runtime `TypeError`**, not just a type error: `fetchAuctionClaimOrders()` returns `applesauceIo.fetchEvents()` results, which carry no `rawEvent` method, so the descriptor input memo threw while rendering and the auction order page never resolved the settlement card or the authority. It is also why the previous head's `e2e-grep` run was red on all five `Order Details - * - Auctions` specs.

**Regression tests added** (RED at the previous head, GREEN here):

- `src/lib/__tests__/settlementDescriptor.test.ts` — a `pending` settlement grants no authority (verified RED: with the validity gate removed the same fixture returns `fulfillmentReady: true`); a fraudulent path release grants none; authority names its canonical claim and authorizes **only** that order id; a sibling order on the same coordinate stays non-fulfillable; the binding helper fails closed on missing/partial authority.
- `src/lib/__tests__/auctionOrderFixture.test.ts` — the same two directions against the production-valid events `seedOrder('auction', …)` actually publishes. This file runs in `bun run test:unit`, so either gate regressing fails on every PR.

**@felixfelix-bot — 2026-08-14, four items** (all `RISK`/`NIT`):

| Item | Status at this head |
|---|---|
| redundant validation in `getAuctionCoordinatesFromOrder` (`getCoordsFromATag` then `isValidATag`) | still open — `orders.tsx:236–244`; the second check is unreachable when the first succeeds |
| `useAuctionBids('', 500, auctionCoordinates \|\| '')` fires with an empty `#a` value on product order views (`OrderDetailComponent.tsx:442`) | still open — three auction hooks (`useAuctionBids`, `useAuctionSettlements`, `useAuctionPathReleases`) are called unconditionally at the top of `OrderDetailComponent` |
| hardcoded `Quantity: 1` in the auction item card | still open — `OrderDetailComponent.tsx:734`; the product branch uses `quantityMap` |
| buyer-view specs use `test.use({ scenario: 'merchant' })` | **not applicable** — `scenario` selects *seeded data*, not the logged-in user. The buyer describes use the `buyerPage` fixture, which authenticates as `devUser2` (`e2e/fixtures/index.ts:54`). The merchant scenario is what seeds the auction order both views read |

### Verification at this head

- `bun run test:unit` → **1386 pass / 0 fail** (94 files), including `src/lib/__tests__/auctionOrderFixture.test.ts`, the production cross-event validator gate on the auction order fixture.
- `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → **335 diagnostics, exactly the `origin/auctions` baseline — 0 new, 5 resolved.** No workflow runs `tsc`, so this was checked by hand against a clean `origin/auctions` worktree. The 5 resolved are the `.rawEvent()` calls above.
- `prettier --check src/ e2e/ AUCTIONS.md` → clean.
- `bunx playwright test e2e/tests/order-detail.spec.ts` → **13 passed (2.4 m)** locally at this head, i.e. the whole `Order Details - Seller/Buyer View - Auctions` family that was red at the previous head.
- Path exercised: `e2e/tests/order-detail.spec.ts` → `e2e/scenarios/index.ts` `seedOrder('auction', …)` → `buildAuctionOrderFixture()` → `assertAuctionOrderFixtureValid()` → `getSettlementDescriptor()` → `getAuctionFulfillmentAuthority()` → `OrderActions`.

### Settlement action buttons — what is gated by what

- **Order surfaces (this PR).** `Process` and `Mark As Shipped` require the authority object *bound to the order being mutated*; `Cancel`/`Confirm Payment Received` are suppressed for auctions; `Receive`/`Complete` (buyer) needs a `PROCESSING`+shipped state that only the authorized seller can produce. The sales/purchases tables (`orderColumns.tsx`) and the auction page's order panel pass no authority, so they stay fail-closed — deliberately, per the review.
- **Auction page (pre-existing, unchanged here).** `Release path & settle` is gated on the canonical winner from the validated bid set plus the local bidder record. `Publish Settlement` still uses a raw-tag path-release check (`hasPathReleaseForTopBid`) rather than `validatePathRelease()`; a forged kind-1025 could therefore *enable* that button, though the settlement it would publish is rejected downstream by the descriptor/validator (a no-op claim, no fund movement). Left as-is to keep this PR scoped; worth its own fix.

### Known coverage gap (pre-existing, unchanged here)

The settlement-status **card content** is not asserted: `order-detail.spec.ts` carries the auction settlement assertion commented out with `TODO: Needs CVM configuration for seeded bid to show up`. The specs therefore prove that an auction order renders as an auction, suppresses the product lifecycle buttons, and transitions through bound claim authority — not the descriptor-derived phase text.

### Open items

1. **Review state.** The previous APPROVED review (@c03rad0r) is anchored to `247f9a25`. The `quality` ruleset is `disabled`, so GitHub does not dismiss it automatically — the badge persists and points at an older commit. **This head needs a fresh review.**
2. **Video evidence.** The recordings/screenshots published earlier were captured at the pre-rebase head; the same flows are re-verified by the 13-spec run at this head. A re-recording can be attached on request.

### Relation to #1144

Complementary. #1144 handles the settlement card on the auction detail page; this PR handles the order details page. Different files, independently mergeable.
